review: Reviewed Ivo's round-57 request 'Assess and recover usable bark' and the World Agent develop review (learning 2): a general assess-and-hand-separate operation for accessible fallen woody material with inspect, separation-trial, recover, resume and cancel modes, reusing probe observation and existing ownership, escrow and work machinery, with an authoritative wood/bark component record, conservation, and no invented tools or favourable backfill. Implemented bark-separation@1 in scope long-ex15 (packages/world-core/src/long-bark-separation.ts, registered in continuous.ts). Inspect (target a visible object or item in reach, own carried items included) runs the baseline open.probe observe unchanged, which is its only charge (1 round, 0.2 energy), and adds a personal unverified record and a bark-separation-inspected event with visible facts only: bark covering, exposed edges at broken ends, piece length, circumference, covered, separated and torn areas, and status composition-unresolved, separability-unresolved, separable-verified, partly-separated, bark-removed, detached-bark or no-material; attached mass and separability stay unknown. Natural piles are reported as not owned work material. Separation-trial (1 round, 0.5 energy) splits exactly 0.1 unit off an owned untreated or partly separated branch stack, lifts and tears that portion's attached bark (recorded waste, 0.011 mass) and reports the accessible edge, hand separation along the grain, areal mass 0.6 and bark share 0.1; the portion keeps its 0.099 wood as its own stack with a separation record, and a per-actor trial record for that source (resource and origin) is kept. Recover needs the actor's own trial on material from the same source, reserves only the selected quantity (0.1 steps, default all) via workCreate/workReserve, and pays 1 round and 1 energy per increment of at most 0.1 m2 of bark surface, including a smaller final increment (workPay); recover pays the first and the same bound action continues; resume pays the next increment after revalidating escrow, record, trial evidence and energy; cancel takes 1 round and no energy and returns the remainder in its actual state; work not continued in a round pauses (afterEnvironment), too little energy pauses before paying, lost or changed material stops the work, death drops the remainder on the ground once; nothing is refunded. Each increment detaches real attached bark: whole 0.03-mass tenths are delivered to an ordinary untreated owned bark stack with the source origin and harvest date (no processing record, so the unchanged simple-shelter@1 and shared-shelter@1 accept whole units, which the tests verify), a sub-tenth remainder is recorded waste, and the reserved branch keeps its wood with mass per unit reduced by exactly the bark removed (0.99 when bare) and a separation record, so the shelters refuse it as treated. A job ledger in the collective work record holds provenance, region, strip pieces (area, width, length, mass, product), products, residual wood, remaining attached bark and waste, and every increment asserts that wood plus attached bark plus recovered bark plus waste equals the processed input. Events: bark-separation-inspected, -trial, -started, -progress, -paused, -resumed, -cancelled, -stopped, -completed. Modeling assumptions, all stated in the interface: branches had no bark representation, so an untreated fallen-branch unit (1.1 mass) is modelled as 0.99 wood plus 0.11 attached bark, reusing the bark-extraction@1 (ex12) 10% outer-bark share; this is a lazily derived composition record, never written onto existing items, and output quantity follows conserved mass on the existing bark unit (0.3 mass), not a unit-for-unit branch-to-bark conversion. Bark area uses the existing bark-unit basis of 0.3 mass per 0.5 m2 (simple-shelter@1 roofing), giving about 0.18 m2 per branch unit; one branch unit is a 2 m piece (as the shelters use it), so bark circumference is about 0.092 m and recovered strips are that wide. All untreated fallen-branch lots share one model with no per-source variation; hand separation at the broken ends works at safe force; water share of the reduced mass follows the branch moisture property as in bark-extraction@1; resource-level fuel and other properties of the peeled branch are not rescaled. Recovered bark becomes the world's single bark resource ('Birch bark' by display name) because every existing recipe consumes that resource; origin keeps its true source. Other woody materials (birch, willow, oak wood, componentLots or otherwise treated stacks) have no represented composition and stay unresolved; trial and recovery are refused there at no cost. Tool-assisted cutting is not implemented; a toolId is refused at no cost. No experience rule is wired: all records are unverified and the completion event carries no qualified flag, so there is no understanding, practice or comfort reward; visualComponents is empty and reusable visual metadata is kept in the job summary. Reuse: open.probe observe and the shared visible-reference resolver, openRemember, collective-work escrow/paid work/stop, material-lots portioning, exact-tenth accounting and the ex15 food-preparation@1 work pattern. This is a real mechanism, not an honest first release: the specification is self-consistent once the stated composition assumption fills the missing representation. Tests cover study, inspection cost and visibility, refusals at no cost, the trial, six-increment recovery of 1.0 bark from 2.9 branch units with mass conservation, pause/resume/cancel, performer-only control, death, and acceptance of a recovered unit by simple-shelter@1 while peeled branches are refused.
